parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the weight of a metre rule using a balancing method. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Place the metre rule on the pivot. Place the load P with its centre on the metre rule at the 90.0 cm mark. Keeping the load P at the 90.0 cm mark, adjust the position of the metre rule on the pivot so that the metre rule is as near as possible to being balanced. Measure, and record in the first row of Table 1.1, the distance a from the 90.0 cm mark to the pivot. Measure, and record in the first row of Table 1.1, the distance b from the pivot to the 50.0 cm mark. Repeat the steps above, placing the centre of the load P at the 85.0 cm, 80.0 cm, 75.0 cm and 70.0 cm marks. Record all values of a and b in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 a / cm b / cm [3]

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text:
a values decreasing all < 25 cm
b values decreasing
all values in cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of a / cm ( y -axis) against b / cm ( x -axis). You do not need to begin your axes at the origin (0, 0). [4]

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
Graph:
Axes correctly labelled with quantity and unit and right way round
Suitable scales
All plots correct to ½ small square
Good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ........................................................ [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Calculate the weight W of the metre rule using the equation W = G × P , where P = 1.0 N. W = ........................................................ [1]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text: Correct calculation, to 2 or 3 significant figures

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text:
Difficulty in achieving exact balance
OR difficulty in judging centre of P
OR load easily slips
OR less than sharp pivot point

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Use the balance provided to measure the mass of the metre rule. mass = ........................................................ [1]
